messages.subject: Moderated Mediation-Probit link, computing conditional simple and indirect effects & plotting
parts:
Hello, 

I am running a second stage moderated mediation model (see below). The main predictor, mediator, and moderator are continuous variables (all mean centered). The outcome variable is binary. 
I need help confirming whether I have correctly coded the computation of the conditional indirect effect, total effects, and proportion mediated. 

Moreover, the interaction term b3*IsolationXSupport in the regression model was statistically significant (CIs did not include 0). I need to compute conditional effects/simple slopes analyses and plot the Probit interaction term. Would I be able to do so in the same model? If so, would you be able to guide me to how I can write the code to get the conditional effects/simple slopes of the b3*IsolationXSupport interaction? Lastly, is there a package I can use to plot these Probit link simple slopes AND the conditional indirect effects of the moderated mediation results (the index of moderated mediation a1*a3 was significant. 

I sincerely thank you for your support and guidance. 

Sincerely, 

Luis

# a path

Isolation_c~ a1*Violence_c 

 

# b paths

Ideation~ cp*Violence_c 

+ b1*Isolation_c #mediator

+ b2*Support_c #moderator 1SDbelow =-1.025341, 1SDabove = 1.025341 

+ b3*IsolationXSupport #interaction term


# Covariances 

Violence_c ~~Violence_c +

+ Support_c +

+ IsolationXSupport
 

Support_c~~Support_c +

IsolationXSupport

IsolationXSupport~~IsolationXSupport

Ideation~~Ideation  #output provides the threshold estimate for ideation

# Intercepts

Violence_c~1

Isolation_c ~1

IsolationXSupport~1

Ideation~1 


# index of moderated mediation

a1b3 := a1*b3

 

# test conditional indirect effects #

mod.belowmean  := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * -1.025341)

mod.atmean        := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * 0)

mod.abovemean := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * 1.025341)

 

# test conditional total effects #

total.belowmean := cp + (a1*b1) + (a1b3 * -1.025341)

total.atmean        := cp + (a1*b1)

total.abovemean := cp + (a1*b1) + (a1b3 * 1.025341)

 

# proportion mediated #

pro.belowmean := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * -1.025341)/cp + (a1*b1) + (a1b3 * -1.025341)

pro.atmean       := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * 0)/cp + (a1*b1)

pro.bovemean  := a1*b1 + (a1b3 * 1.025341)/cp + (a1*b1) + (a1b3 * 1.025341)


'

# fit model  

fit14=lavaan(modmediation14, data=data1, ordered=c('Ideation'), estimator='DWLS', se = 'bootstrap', bootstrap=10000L,  link = "probit", fixed.x=FALSE, auto.var = TRUE, meanstructure=TRUE)

Hi Terrence, 

I have a question regarding the probit threshold or intercept for a moderated mediation model using probit link regression to account for a binary outcome (ideation, 0=No, 1=Yes). 


The code below automatically provides a threshold estimate (ideation|t1 = -0.161): 

fit14a=lavaan(modmediation14a, data=data1, ordered=c('ideation'), estimator='DWLS', se = 'bootstrap', bootstrap=10000L,  link = "probit", fixed.x=FALSE, auto.var = TRUE, meanstructure=TRUE)


Because the command above yields a probit threshold,  I am unsure whether I need to command lavaan to provide an intercept for the binary outcome variable (ideation~1)? 

I am confused about this because I notice that the model fit indices sometimes worsen when I include ideation~1  in the code. I also notice that when I have a saturated model, the df = -1. Does the code below automatically account one parameter pertaining to the probit threshold?   


Thank you in advance for your help and clarifications.

messages.subject: Re: Moderated Mediation-Probit link, computing conditional simple and indirect effects & plotting
parts:
Because the command above yields a probit threshold,  I am unsure whether I need to command lavaan to provide an intercept for the binary outcome variable (ideation~1)? 

I am confused about this because I notice that the model fit indices sometimes worsen when I include ideation~1  in the code. I also notice that when I have a saturated model, the df = -1. Does the code below automatically account one parameter pertaining to the probit threshold?

The model is not identified if you try to estimate both.  By default, it will estimate the threshold and fix the intercept to zero, whereas most GLM software (e.g., R's glm() function) does the opposite.   If you want to switch it around, you can estimate the intercept, but you would also have to fix the threshold to zero:

ideation | 0*t1

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Moderated Mediation-Probit link, computing conditional simple and indirect effects & plotting
parts: Is probit link applied to all paths even when a path is between two continuous variables?
No, a link function is specific to the outcome variable.
X --> M (path a1): this is a regression among two continuous variables (Does path a1 get tested with probit link or OLS?)
Neither, it is a ML estimate of a linear effect of X on M (with an identity link for M).

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated Mediation-Probit link, computing conditional simple and indirect effects & plotting
parts: When computing the indirect effect, what values is lavaan using to calculate the product of the indirect effect (a1*b1)
See your summary() output.  The parameter estimates with those labels are what lavaan multiplies, because that is what you told it to do.
when a1 is an ML estimation and b1 is a probit link estimation?

I misspoke.  lavaan uses DWLS estimation, so they are both (weighted) least-squares estimates (but not ordinary/unweighted least squares).  If you set estimator="PML", you can get ML estimates of both.  The estimator applies to all parameters in the model, not each parameter separately.

I am assuming that the unstandardized b and standardized B in the output for the ML estimate and the probit link estimates will be interpreted differently (e.g., a1 (ML): the mean of M changes for every unit change of the predictor; b1, direct and indirect effects (probit): the amount of z-score change in the outcome for every one unit change in the predictor)?

The interpretations (and link functions) do not depend on the estimator.  The (un)standardized estimates involving endogenous ordered variables are interpreted in terms of their latent response distributions, which are z-scores by default (parameterization="delta").  For binary outcomes, you can usually think of this as a latent propensity for being in the "higher" category.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
